**Overview**
This Intellectual Property Agreement (May 12, 2020) among Marv Enterprises, Premier Biomedical, and Technology Health, Inc. (“THI”) assigns Premier’s exclusive patent rights to THI and grants THI an exclusive worldwide license to COVID-19-related patent applications in Appendix A.

**Main Obligations for Us (THI)**
- **Up-front and milestone payments:** ~$80k to Marv by July 20, 2020; $40k to Premier; $150k stock purchase; 50,000 THI shares to Premier.
- **Royalties:** 5% of Fair Market Value of licensed products/services to Marv quarterly, plus a separate 5% annual royalty stream to Premier shareholders until $40M is paid.
- **IP cost reimbursement:** Prepayment of all patent prosecution costs; failure to prepay causes country-by-country reversion to Marv.
- **Joint venture funding:** $750k by June 20, 2020; $1.15M by July 30, 2020; $500k to a U.K. subsidiary—all for COVID-19 development.
- **Quarterly reporting:** Certified statements of sales, services, and royalties within 30 days after each quarter.
- **Legal fees:** Reimbursement of Marv’s legal expenses.
- **Late fees:** 3% over prime on overdue amounts (capped at the legal maximum).

**Key Risks**
- **Reversion triggers:** Missing the license-fee or joint-venture payment deadlines causes the exclusive license to revert to Premier (with only a proportionate product interest retained if the $2M JV funding is short).
- **No minimum royalty floor:** THI has no minimum annual royalty, but the $40M cap on the Premier shareholder royalty is a long-term cost exposure.
- **No liability cap:** There is no aggregate cap on damages or liability, and no carve-out language either.
- **Broad exclusivity:** The license is exclusive worldwide, limiting freedom to operate with alternative partners.
- **IP cost exposure:** THI must affirm and prepay prosecution costs for each country; any denial or non-payment reverts rights to Marv.

- **Warrant preservation clause:** 150 million THI stock warrants previously issued to Mitchell S. Felder cannot be cancelled or altered without his specific request—an unusual personal benefit for a counterparty’s principal.
- **Joint venture payments to THI itself:** THI is required to pay itself/the U.K. subsidiary for R&D, creating circular funding obligations that may complicate accounting.
- **Non-exclusive engagement:** Despite the exclusive license, the agreement explicitly states the relationship is a “nonexclusive engagement/venture,” which is atypical for an exclusive patent license.

**What to Monitor**
- Payment deadlines (license fee, JV milestones, IP cost prepayments) to avoid reversion.
- Quarterly royalty calculations and certified reports for accuracy.
- Prosecution of Appendix A patents and election of countries within the 90-day window.
- Any amendments to the underlying 2010/2020 Agreements that could affect rights.
- Status of the 150M warrants and related insider obligations.

**Contract Intake Review: Andy North Endorsement Agreement**

**Overview:** Two-year worldwide endorsement (Feb. 21, 2011 – Dec. 31, 2012). Company pays guaranteed fees ($55K/$70K), a 1% royalty on all gross revenue, and expenses, in exchange for an exclusive license to use Andy North’s likeness/endorsement for F2 golf clubs.

**Main Obligations for Company:**
- Pay guaranteed fees and 1% quarterly royalty on all Company Product gross revenue (§6–7).
- Reimburse first-class travel, hotel, and ground transport for appearances (§5.f).
- Supply free endorsed products for North’s personal use (§7.g).
- Obtain and maintain $2M A++ general liability insurance naming North as insured (§16).
- Submit all advertising materials to North for approval; cannot use disapproved materials (§8).
- Broadly indemnify North for claims arising from product use, advertising, and Company breaches (§15).

**Key Risks:**
- **Uncapped liability:** The indemnification in §15 covers personal injury, death, property damage, and advertising claims with no monetary cap on Company’s exposure.
- **Audit exposure:** North may audit books/records for two years post-termination; if underpayment exceeds 5% for any quarter, Company reimburses inspection costs (§7.c).
- **Post-termination restrictions:** Upon expiration/termination, Company cannot use or distribute any advertising materials or sell/ship new product bearing North’s likeness, except existing retail-channel inventory (§3).
- **No termination for convenience:** Contract is terminable only for material breach, non-payment, or bankruptcy (§12–13).
- **Anti-assignment:** Assignment requires North’s prior written consent, which may impede M&A activity (§19).

**Unusual Provisions:**
- Royalties apply to “all Gross Revenue generated from the sale of all Company Products,” not merely endorsed products (§7.b), expanding the royalty base beyond typical endorsement deals.
- North must use the F2 golf bag at public events but may place up to two non-competitive third-party logos on it (§6.b).
- SAG/AFTRA dues and assessments are fully Company-funded without offset (§10).

**What to Monitor:**
- Quarterly royalty calculations and reporting accuracy given the broad base.
- Maintenance of the $2M insurance policy and delivery of proof to North.
- Written approval for all advertising materials before use.
- Pipeline inventory of product with North’s likeness as the term nears expiration.
- North’s public appearances to confirm no competitive endorsement activity.

- Developer is explicitly “not penalized” if basic reporting features slip to Phase 2, weakening commitment.
- Platform design includes “only one dispensary per zip code,” a business exclusivity rule that could raise antitrust scrutiny.

Monitoring:

- Track milestone deliverables against acceptance criteria before releasing payments.

**Contract Intake Review: HDS – Paul Silas Endorsement Agreement**

**Overview.** One-year endorsement (Feb 2012 – Feb 2013) under which HDS acquired rights to use Paul Silas’s name and likeness to promote Clotamin in three TV markets, online, and in press releases.

**Our Main Obligations.**
- Pay $50,000 (via agent CSE) on a fixed schedule, plus $5,000 per additional market, and fund first-class travel and lodging for Silas and one representative.
- Provide a one-year supply of Clotamin (365 caplets).
- Maintain CGL ($1M/$2M), umbrella ($5M), and media liability ($2M) insurance naming Silas as additional insured, with 30-day cancellation notice.
- Indemnify Silas and his agents/employees for product liability, IP infringement, and claims arising from our advertising or breach, except for Silas’s active negligence or willful misconduct.
- Obtain Silas’s prior written approval for all advertising materials and press releases; non-response within five business days is deemed unapproved.

**Key Risks.**
- **Uncapped indemnity.** Our indemnity obligation is broad and has no monetary cap. Coupled with product-liability exposure, this creates significant contingent liability.
- **Anti-assignment.** The agreement prohibits assignment without Silas’s prior written consent. If the acquisition was structured as an asset purchase or merger, we may need to obtain his consent to avoid a breach.
- **Celebrity termination leverage.** Silas can terminate for our insolvency, payment default (with a short 3-day cure), or breach. Upon such termination we remain liable for all consideration due, while our usage rights terminate immediately.
- **Approval bottleneck.** The deemed-unapproved mechanism if Silas/CSE does not respond within five business days could delay campaigns.

**Unusual Provisions.**
- The $25,000 production fee becomes non-refundable once the production session is scheduled, even if the session never occurs.
- Silas is named to a “Board of Advisors” but has no actual advisory duties beyond being listed as a brand ambassador.

**Monitoring Items.**
- Track payment deadlines and manage production-fee timing.
- Maintain insurance coverage and deliver certificates upon request.
- Submit all advertising materials for approval well before launch dates.
- Confirm the acquisition structure did not trigger the anti-assignment clause; if it did, secure Silas’s consent.
- Monitor Silas’s compliance with the exclusivity / non-compete (no other multivitamin endorsements).

- No minimum volume commitment despite firm service status.
